name: Crypto wash-sale check
pitch: Explain the wash sale rule for crypto and check your transaction history for violations.
instructions: Start by searching the web for a plain English explanation of the crypto wash‑sale rule. When you have the rule, read the person's transaction history files. Look for any crypto sales that happened within 30 days of a purchase of the same token. If you find matching sales and purchases, list them in a table with the dates, amounts and whether each is a violation. If no violations are found, say so. If any file is missing or the rule cannot be confirmed, tell the person what you could not check and ask if they want you to look elsewhere.
starters: Check my transaction history for violations

examples.does: Search the web for the rule and give a short plain‑English summary.

examples.ask: Check my transaction history for violations
examples.does: Read the transaction files, compare sales and purchases within 30 days, and show any violations in a table.

skills.name: explain-crypto-wash-sale
skills.description: Summarise the crypto wash‑sale rule in plain English.
skills.body: 1. Search the web for 'crypto wash‑sale rule'. 2. Read the top result. 3. Write 2‑3 short sentences in your own words: what the rule is, why it exists, and the 30‑day window. 4. If the search fails, say you could not find a clear explanation and ask if they want you to try another source.

skills.name: check-transactions-for-violations
skills.description: Scan transaction files for crypto wash‑sale violations.
skills.body: 1. List the files in the workspace. 2. Read each file that looks like a transaction log (csv, json, txt). 3. For every crypto sale, look for a purchase of the same token within the previous 30 days. 4. Collect all matches. 5. If matches exist, create a table with the sale date, purchase date, token name, and amounts. 6. If no matches exist, say no violations were found. 7. If a file cannot be read, say which file and ask if they want you to check another.

readme:
# Crypto wash‑sale check

Explains the crypto wash‑sale rule and scans your transaction history for violations. Works with CSV or JSON transaction logs on your computer.

**What it needs:** web_search to find the rule, file_read to look at your logs, show_table to display any violations.

**What it will not do:** It will not give tax advice, it will not move money, and it will not report to any tax authority.
